$(\widehat S_d,\widehat P,\widehat\Sigma)$ be a reference finite element

freedom are bounded on $W^{\ell,p}(\widehat S_d)$ for an integer

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $k\ge1$, $1\le p\le\infty$ and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Let $U,V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open
and let $\Phi:U\to V$ be a $C^k$ diffeomorphism with inverse
$\Psi:=\Phi^{-1}:V\to U$. Fix open sets $U_0\subset\subset U$ and
$V_0\subset\subset V$ with $\Phi(U_0)\subseteq V_0$, and suppose that on
$\overline{U_0}$ the derivatives of $\Phi$ through order $k$ are bounded and
that on $\overline{V_0}$ the derivatives of $\Psi$ through order $k$ are
bounded; in the situation of
[[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]] these are exactly the compact
patches on which the flattening chart and its inverse have bounded derivatives
through order $k$. Then:

1. for every $u\in W^{k,p}(V_0;\mathbb K)$ the composition
$u\circ\Phi$ belongs to $W^{k,p}(U_0;\mathbb K)$, and for every
$1\le|\alpha|\le k$ its weak derivatives satisfy, almost everywhere on
$U_0$,
$$D^\alpha(u\circ\Phi)=\sum_{1\le|\beta|\le|\alpha|}\bigl((D^\beta u)\circ\Phi\bigr)\,P_{\alpha\beta}\bigl(D\Phi,\dots,D^k\Phi\bigr),$$
where $P_{\alpha\beta}$ is a universal polynomial with integer coefficients,
whose values on $\overline{U_0}$ are bounded by a constant depending only on
$n,k$ and the stated bounds for $\Phi$;

2. there is a constant $C$, depending only on $n$, $k$, $p$ and the two sets of
chart bounds, with
$$\|u\circ\Phi\|_{W^{k,p}(U_0)}\le C\,\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(V_0)}\qquad\text{for all }u\in W^{k,p}(V_0;\mathbb K).$$
If in addition $\Psi(V_0)\subseteq U_0$ (equivalently, under the stated
$\Phi(U_0)\subseteq V_0$, $\Phi(U_0)=V_0$), the same assertion holds for
composition with $\Psi$ from $W^{k,p}(U_0)$ to $W^{k,p}(V_0)$.

For $k=1$ only the first derivatives of $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ enter, so bounded
$C^1$ chart and inverse data suffice; no $C^1$-only claim is made for $k>1$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $N\in\mathbb N_0$, choose
$x_1,\ldots,x_N\in\overline{\widehat S_d}$, and let
$\ell\ge1$ be an integer. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $\ell>d/p$, then each
point evaluation has a unique continuous-representative value and
$$|u(x_j)|\le C\|u\|_{W^{\ell,p}(\widehat S_d)}.$$
If $p=\infty$, the same conclusion holds for every $\ell\ge1$.
Consequently any finite set of Lagrange nodal evaluations is bounded on
the stated Sobolev space and defines a well-defined degree-of-freedom
functional there. No boundedness at $\ell=d/p$ is asserted.

citations.quote: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded Lebesgue-measurable domain of finite positive measure. Let $\mathcal S=(S_i)_{i=1}^m$ and $\mathcal T=(T_j)_{j=1}^n$ be finite measurable partitions of $\Omega$ up to null sets, with disjoint interiors modulo null sets and positive cell volumes. Define exact overlap weights $w_{ji}=|T_j\cap S_i|$. For source constants $v_i$, the intersection-volume remap is the target piecewise-constant field $Rv$ whose value on $T_j$ is $ (Rv)_j=|T_j|^{-1}\sum_i w_{ji}v_i$. All weights are exact measures; an approximate clipping weight is not silently substituted.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be
conjugate exponents, and let $f,g$ be measurable real-valued functions.

1. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $q<\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^q(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q.$$
2. If $p=1$ and $q=\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$ and
   $g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_1\|g\|_\infty.$$
3. If $p=\infty$ and $q=1$ with $f\in L^\infty(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_1.$$

In every case the right-hand side is finite, so $fg$ is integrable.

The class $L^1(\mu)$ is a complex vector space, and the Lebesgue integral is
complex-linear on it:
$$\int (\alpha f+\beta g)\,d\mu=\alpha\int f\,d\mu+\beta\int g\,d\mu \qquad(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb C,\ f,g\in L^1(\mu)).$$

derivations.claim: By [F4], Lebesgue measure is countably additive and hence finitely additive. The partition hypotheses therefore give $\sum_iw_{ji}=|T_j|$ for every target cell and $\sum_jw_{ji}=|S_i|$ for every source cell; omitted partition boundaries are null and do not change these measures. The same finite additivity gives $\int_{T_j}v=\sum_iw_{ji}v_i$.
For any target cellwise-constant $z$, sum over target cells: $\int_\Omega(v-Rv)z=\sum_j z_j(\sum_iw_{ji}v_i-|T_j|(Rv)_j)=0$ by [F1] and step 1.1. Thus $v-Rv$ is orthogonal to the target subspace.

Orthogonality with $z=Rv$ gives $\|v\|_2^2=\|Rv\|_2^2+\|v-Rv\|_2^2$, so $\|Rv\|_2\le\|v\|_2$. All terms are finite because the partitions are finite, cells have finite volume, and $v$ is piecewise constant.

By the column-sum identity in step 1.1, $\int Rv=\sum_j|T_j|(Rv)_j=\sum_i|S_i|v_i=\int v$. If each $v_i\ge0$, every overlap weight is nonnegative, so the defining finite weighted average is nonnegative.

Fix an integer $d\ge2$. The **reference open simplex** is
$$\widehat S_d:=\{\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d:\widehat x_i>0\ (1\le i\le d),\ \sum_{i=1}^d\widehat x_i<1\},$$
with closure $\overline{\widehat S_d}=\operatorname{conv}\{0,e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$.

A **matching affine simplicial mesh** of a bounded polyhedral open set
$\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ is a finite set $\mathcal T$ of closed,
nondegenerate $d$-simplices such that their union is $\overline\Omega$,
their interiors are pairwise disjoint, $\Omega$ is the interior of their
union, and the intersection of two distinct cells is either empty or a
whole face of each. Thus no lower-dimensional crack is omitted from
$\Omega$ while its surrounding cells are retained. Every interior facet is
incident to exactly two cells and every boundary facet to one. The faces of
a cell are the convex hulls of its vertex subsets. A facet means a face of
dimension $d-1$.

For each cell $K\in\mathcal T$, an affine bijection
$$F_K:\overline{\widehat S_d}\to K,\qquad F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x,$$
with invertible $A_K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is a **reference map**.
Choose the vertex order so $\det A_K>0$; this is the orientation convention
used for Piola formulas. Write $h_K:=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and let
$\rho_K$ be the radius of the largest Euclidean ball contained in $K$.
A family $\{\mathcal T_h\}_{h\in H}$ is **shape regular** if there is a
finite $\sigma$ such that $h_K/\rho_K\le\sigma$ for every
$h\in H$ and $K\in\mathcal T_h$. This universal condition is vacuous for
an empty family.
This definition uses radius; references using the diameter of the inscribed
ball differ by a factor of two.

An affine image of the reference square is a parallelogram. A general
quadrilateral requires a nonaffine map and is outside this affine definition;
curved-cell approximation is not included here.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

derivations.claim: Direct differentiation gives $D\Phi=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\x/2&1\end{pmatrix}$ and determinant $1$; the stated inverse is verified by substitution. On a triangle with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_i$ and vertex first-coordinates $x_i$, exact quadratic expansion gives $I_h(x^2/4)-x^2/4=\frac14\sum_{i<j}\lambda_i\lambda_j(x_i-x_j)^2$. Since $|x_i-x_j|\le h_K$ and $0\le\lambda_i\le1$, this is bounded by $Ch_K^2$.

Differentiating the barycentric expression in step 1.1, only the factors $\lambda_i\lambda_j$ vary; their derivatives are bounded by $C h_K^{-1}$ using [F2], while $|x_i-x_j|^2\le h_K^2$. The product rule therefore gives a derivative bound $Ch_K$. Thus $\|D(I_h(x^2/4)-x^2/4)\|_{L^\infty(K)}\le Ch_K$, yielding the global $Ch$ derivative estimate and the $Ch^2$ value estimate. By [F3] these are the geometry errors $e_1$ and $e_0$.

The first coordinate of $\Phi_h$ is $x$, and on each vertical segment its second coordinate is the continuous piecewise-affine function $y+I_h(x^2/4)(x,y)$. Its slope on every subsegment is $1+\partial_y I_h(x^2/4)\ge1-Ch$. Choose $h$ with $Ch\le1/2$. Integration over the finitely many subsegments makes this coordinate strictly increasing with increment at least half the vertical increment. Equal images must therefore have equal first coordinates and then equal second-coordinate inputs; hence $\Phi_h$ is injective. The same derivative estimate gives $\det D\Phi_h=1+\partial_yI_h(x^2/4)\ge1/2$.

Define $e_0=\|\Phi-\Phi_h\|_{L^\infty(\widehat\Omega)}$ and $e_1=\|D\Phi-D\Phi_h\|_{L^\infty(\widehat\Omega;op)}$. A geometry approximation claim must separately state bounds on $e_0,e_1$, both Jacobian lower bounds, and boundary-trace compatibility; none follows from the word “isoparametric.”

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded Lebesgue-measurable domain of finite positive measure. Let $\mathcal S=(S_i)_{i=1}^m$ and $\mathcal T=(T_j)_{j=1}^n$ be finite measurable partitions of $\Omega$ up to null sets, with disjoint interiors modulo null sets and positive cell volumes. Define exact overlap weights $w_{ji}=|T_j\cap S_i|$. For source constants $v_i$, the intersection-volume remap is the target piecewise-constant field $Rv$ whose value on $T_j$ is $ (Rv)_j=|T_j|^{-1}\sum_i w_{ji}v_i$. All weights are exact measures; an approximate clipping weight is not silently substituted.

Assume Countable Choice. Under the finite partition hypotheses of [[def-intersection-volume-conservative-remapping]], let $P_0(\mathcal T)$ be the target cellwise-constant subspace of $L^2(\Omega)$. For every source piecewise-constant $v$, $Rv$ is the $L^2$ orthogonal projection of $v$ onto $P_0(\mathcal T)$, hence $\|Rv\|_2\le\|v\|_2$. It preserves total mass, $\int_\Omega Rv=\int_\Omega v$, and if all $v_i\ge0$ then every target value $(Rv)_j\ge0$.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be
conjugate exponents, and let $f,g$ be measurable real-valued functions.

1. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $q<\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^q(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q.$$
2. If $p=1$ and $q=\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$ and
   $g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_1\|g\|_\infty.$$
3. If $p=\infty$ and $q=1$ with $f\in L^\infty(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_1.$$

In every case the right-hand side is finite, so $fg$ is integrable.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: The Lipschitz condition gives $|u(\Phi(X))-u(\Phi_h(X))|\le L_ue_0$ for every $X$. Integrating its square against $J_h\le J^*$ gives the geometry term $L_ue_0\sqrt{J^*|\widehat\Omega|}$.

For any $q\in L^2(\Omega_h)$ and target cell $T$, [F3] gives $|T||P_Tq|_T^2=|\int_Tq|^2/|T|\le\int_T|q|^2$. Summing over the disjoint target cells shows $P_T$ is contractive. The same averaging identity gives $q-P_Tq$ orthogonal to every target-cellwise constant, so $P_T$ is the orthogonal projection.

By [F2], $Rv_S=P_Tv_S$. Thus $u-Rv_S=(u-P_Tu)+P_T(u-v_S)$; the two terms are orthogonal and $P_T$ is contractive by step 1.2. The first term has norm $\eta_T$ and the second is at most $\eta_S$, whence $\|u-Rv_S\|_{L^2(\Omega_h)}\le\eta_T+\eta_S$.

Apply [F4] separately on the finitely many mesh cells to identify the physical $L^2(\Omega_h)$ norm in step 2.1 with the weighted pullback norm of $(u-Rv_S)\circ\Phi_h$. The triangle inequality with step 1.1 proves the claimed bound.

Fix a compatible labeled initial mesh. Recursive reference-edge closure of any finite marked set terminates, produces a matching conforming NVB descendant, and preserves the shape bound of [[lem-afem-nvb-shape-regularity-and-three-generation-properties]]. For a sequence of such refinements in which each selected cell is first requested for three uniform generations, there is a constant $C_{\rm cl}$ depending only on the initial mesh such that
$$\#\mathcal T_n-\#\mathcal T_0\le C_{\rm cl}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\#M_k.$$
The constant is for the cumulative sequence; no uniform bound on the added cells in one single refinement call is asserted.

Fix a reference matching affine simplicial mesh as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]]. An admissible curved cell is the image of a closed reference simplex $\widehat K$ under a map $F_K\in C^2(\widehat K;\mathbb R^d)$ that extends to a diffeomorphism on a neighborhood, is orientation preserving, and satisfies $0<j_0\le J_K:=\det DF_K\le j_1$ and $\|DF_K\|+\|(DF_K)^{-1}\|+\|D^2F_K\|\le C_F$. The physical cells have disjoint interiors, cover the domain up to their shared facets, and maps agree on each common reference facet under the prescribed affine facet identification. Define the volume metric $G_K=DF_K^TDF_K$, volume factor $J_K=\sqrt{\det G_K}$, and for a reference facet parametrization $\widehat f$ the surface metric $G_{K,\widehat f}=D(F_K\circ\widehat f)^TD(F_K\circ\widehat f)$ and surface factor $\sqrt{\det G_{K,\widehat f}}$. The positive-Jacobian lower bound is the admissibility certificate; it is not inferred from a drawing or from Delaunay quality.

derivations.claim: Apply [F1] to the finite request. Its output is a conforming affine triangulation, so each interior edge is represented by the same complete reference segment from both incident cells; no hanging edge subdivision remains.

On a common edge, the assumed geometry map has one trace from the shared reference segment. By [F2] the two incident curved-cell parametrizations use that same trace, and injectivity prevents distinct reference interfaces from being identified as overlapping physical interiors. Thus the physical curved interface matches.

Assume Countable Choice, as in
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]] and
[[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]]. For an open set
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge1$, an integer $k\ge0$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, set
$$H^k(\Omega;\mathbb K):=W^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The elements are the same almost-everywhere classes, and their weak
derivatives and norm are exactly those already defined for $W^{k,2}$. When the
scalar field is fixed, write $H^k(\Omega)$.

The notation $H^k_0(\Omega)$ is reserved for the later definition by closure of
compactly supported smooth functions in the Sobolev norm. This item assigns no
boundary values to an equivalence class and asserts no characterization by
pointwise vanishing or by traces.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p\le\infty$, and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Write
$$\mathcal A_k=\{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n:|\alpha|\le k\}.$$
This is a finite nonempty set: every coordinate of such an $\alpha$ lies in
$\{0,\ldots,k\}$, and it contains the zero multi-index.

The real and complex $L^p$ classes use the conventions in
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]. Their quotient
norm values are supplied by
[[thm-the-l-p-norm-descends-to-the-quotient-and-makes-l-p-a-normed-space]]
for real scalars and
[[thm-complex-holder-minkowski-and-the-quotient-norm]] for complex scalars.

Define $W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ to be the set of classes
$u\in L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ such that, for every $\alpha\in\mathcal A_k$,
there is an $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ class with a locally integrable
representative $v_\alpha$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v_\alpha\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Here the weak derivative is the one in
[[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]. Under
[[def-countable-choice]], local integrability of $L^p$ representatives and
invariance under null-set changes follow from
[[lem-weak-derivative-is-independent-of-lp-representatives]], while
[[lem-weak-derivatives-are-unique-almost-everywhere]] gives uniqueness of each
locally integrable derivative class. Thus this condition is a condition on the
$L^p$ class $u$, and each resulting derivative determines one $L^p$ class,
denoted $D^\alpha u$. The test pairing is bilinear, without conjugation.

For the zero multi-index, set $D^0u=u$. Since $\mathcal A_0=\{0\}$,
$$W^{0,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)=L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
The Sobolev norm expression is
$$\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}= \begin{cases} \left(\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}^p\right)^{1/p},&1\le p<\infty,\\[1ex] \displaystyle\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_k} \|D^\alpha u\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},&p=\infty. \end{cases}$$
The formula is finite because each derivative class belongs to $L^p$ and
$\mathcal A_k$ is finite; at $k=0$ it reduces to the $L^p$ norm expression.
The finite maximum is defined because $\mathcal A_k$ is nonempty. The norm
axioms for this expression are a separate assertion from this definition.

For open $U\subseteq\Omega$ with $\overline U$ compact and contained in
$\Omega$, the notation $W^{k,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ means that
the restriction of the class belongs to $W^{k,p}(U;\mathbb K)$ for every such
$U$.

If $\Omega=\varnothing$, the $L^p$ space and every $W^{k,p}$ space contain
only the zero class, and the displayed norm expression is zero.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Fix an integer $d\ge2$. The **reference open simplex** is
$$\widehat S_d:=\{\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d:\widehat x_i>0\ (1\le i\le d),\ \sum_{i=1}^d\widehat x_i<1\},$$
with closure $\overline{\widehat S_d}=\operatorname{conv}\{0,e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$.

A **matching affine simplicial mesh** of a bounded polyhedral open set
$\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ is a finite set $\mathcal T$ of closed,
nondegenerate $d$-simplices such that their union is $\overline\Omega$,
their interiors are pairwise disjoint, $\Omega$ is the interior of their
union, and the intersection of two distinct cells is either empty or a
whole face of each. Thus no lower-dimensional crack is omitted from
$\Omega$ while its surrounding cells are retained. Every interior facet is
incident to exactly two cells and every boundary facet to one. The faces of
a cell are the convex hulls of its vertex subsets. A facet means a face of
dimension $d-1$.

For each cell $K\in\mathcal T$, an affine bijection
$$F_K:\overline{\widehat S_d}\to K,\qquad F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x,$$
with invertible $A_K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is a **reference map**.
Choose the vertex order so $\det A_K>0$; this is the orientation convention
used for Piola formulas. Write $h_K:=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and let
$\rho_K$ be the radius of the largest Euclidean ball contained in $K$.
A family $\{\mathcal T_h\}_{h\in H}$ is **shape regular** if there is a
finite $\sigma$ such that $h_K/\rho_K\le\sigma$ for every
$h\in H$ and $K\in\mathcal T_h$. This universal condition is vacuous for
an empty family.
This definition uses radius; references using the diameter of the inscribed
ball differ by a factor of two.

An affine image of the reference square is a parallelogram. A general
quadrilateral requires a nonaffine map and is outside this affine definition;
curved-cell approximation is not included here.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x$ map the fixed reference simplex
$\widehat S_d$ bijectively to a cell $K$ of a shape-regular family, and let
$h_K$ be its diameter and $\rho_K$ its inradius. There are constants
$c,C>0$, depending only on $d$, the reference simplex, and the shape
regularity bound, such that
$$c h_K\le s_{\min}(A_K)\le \|A_K\|\le C h_K, \qquad c h_K^d\le\det A_K\le C h_K^d.$$
For each facet $F$, its affine surface Jacobian is comparable to
$h_K^{d-1}$, and its altitude from the opposite vertex is comparable to
$h_K$. Thus Sobolev scaling constants can be expressed using $h_K$ alone,
with constants uniform over the family.

Let $\widehat\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded reference domain and let $\Phi,\Phi_h:\overline{\widehat\Omega}\to\mathbb R^d$ be cellwise $C^2$ admissible maps with matching traces, positive Jacobians, and common image topology. The exact and approximate domains are $\Omega=\Phi(\widehat\Omega)$ and $\Omega_h=\Phi_h(\widehat\Omega)$. Define $e_0=\|\Phi-\Phi_h\|_{L^\infty(\widehat\Omega)}$ and $e_1=\|D\Phi-D\Phi_h\|_{L^\infty(\widehat\Omega;op)}$. A geometry approximation claim must separately state bounds on $e_0,e_1$, both Jacobian lower bounds, and boundary-trace compatibility; none follows from the word “isoparametric.”

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\widehat\Omega=[-1,1]^2$, let $\mathcal T_h$ be a matching shape-regular affine triangulation, and put $\Phi(x,y)=(x,y+x^2/4)$. Let $I_h$ be the vertexwise P1 interpolant and $\Phi_h(x,y)=(x,y+I_h(x^2/4))$. In the notation of [[def-curved-domain-geometry-approximation]], there is a constant $C$ depending only on the shape-regularity bound such that $e_0\le Ch^2$ and $e_1\le Ch$. For sufficiently small $h$, $\det D\Phi_h\ge1/2$, and $\Phi_h$ is globally one-to-one on the square. The exact map has $\det D\Phi=1$ and a global inverse $(X,Y)\mapsto(X,Y-X^2/4)$.

Let $\Phi,\Phi_h$ be the orientation-preserving maps of [[def-curved-domain-geometry-approximation]], with $J,J_h\ge j_*>0$ and $\|D\Phi\|_\infty+\|D\Phi_h\|_\infty\le M$. Set $B=J D\Phi^{-1}D\Phi^{-T}$ and $B_h=J_hD\Phi_h^{-1}D\Phi_h^{-T}$. Then $\|B-B_h\|_\infty\le C e_1$, where $C$ depends only on $d,j_*,M$. Consequently $|\int_{\widehat\Omega}
abla v^T(B-B_h)
abla w|\le C e_1\|
abla v\|_2\|
abla w\|_2$ for $v,w\in H^1(\widehat\Omega)$.

Assume AC and Countable Choice. In dimension two let $K=\Psi(\widetilde K)$, where $\widetilde K$ is a shape-regular affine triangle of diameter comparable to $h_K$, and $\Psi$ extends to a $C^2$ diffeomorphism on a neighborhood of $\overline{\widetilde K}$. Assume $\|D\Psi\|_\infty+\|D\Psi^{-1}\|_\infty+\|D^2\Psi\|_\infty+\|J_\Psi^{-1}\|_\infty$ are uniformly bounded. Let $v$ denote its continuous representative and set $I_Kv=(I_{\widetilde K}(v\circ\Psi))\circ\Psi^{-1}$, the mapped nodal P1 interpolant. For $v\in H^2(K)$, $\|v-I_Kv\|_{L^2(K)}\le C h_K^2\|v\|_{H^2(K)}$ and $|v-I_Kv|_{H^1(K)}\le C h_K\|v\|_{H^2(K)}$, with $C$ uniform over the family.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let
$\Omega=(-1,1)^2$ have a finite matching affine triangular mesh, and let
$u\in H^2(\Omega;\mathbb R)\cap H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb R)$. On each triangle
take the unique continuous representative of the restriction of $u$. These
representatives give one well-defined value at every mesh vertex. The global
nodal P1 interpolant $I_hu$, affine on each triangle and equal to these values
at its vertices, is continuous, has zero trace on every boundary edge, and
belongs to $H^1_0(\Omega)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, $a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ a bounded coercive form with boundedness constant $M$ and coercivity constant $\alpha>0$, and $F:V\to\mathbb K$ a bounded functional linear in the real case and conjugate-linear in the complex test argument. Let $V_h\subseteq V$ be finite-dimensional, and let $a_h:V_h\times V_h\to\mathbb K$ and $F_h:V_h\to\mathbb K$ be bounded, with $F_h$ having the same test-linearity as $F$, and $a_h$ coercive with constant $\alpha_h>0$ in the inherited norm. Both $a$ and $a_h$ are sesquilinear (bilinear over $\mathbb R$), linear in their first argument and conjugate-linear in their second over $\mathbb C$. There are unique exact and discrete solutions $u$ and $u_h$, and

$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\left((1+M/\alpha_h)\|u-v_h\|_V+\frac{\delta_{a,h}(v_h)+\delta_{F,h}}{\alpha_h}\right),$$

where the defects are those of [[def-variational-crime-error-framework]]. For a family of meshes this is a uniform estimate whenever $\inf_h\alpha_h>0$ and the displayed approximation and defect terms are uniformly controlled. The term $\delta_{F,h}$ retains source approximation and data oscillation.

Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. In the **exact variational problem**, $V$ is a Hilbert space, $a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ is a bounded coercive sesquilinear form (bilinear when $\mathbb K=\mathbb R$), linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second when $\mathbb K=\mathbb C$, and $F:V\to\mathbb K$ is bounded and has the same linearity in its test argument as the second argument of $a$. Exact solutions satisfy $a(u,v)=F(v)$ for every $v\in V$. Boundedness and coercivity have the meanings in [[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]].

For a **conforming perturbed Galerkin problem**, $V_h\subseteq V$ is a finite-dimensional subspace, $a_h:V_h\times V_h\to\mathbb K$ and $F_h:V_h\to\mathbb K$ are the discrete form and load, and $u_h\in V_h$ solves $a_h(u_h,w_h)=F_h(w_h)$. Its discrete coercivity constant is any $\alpha_h>0$ such that $\operatorname{Re}a_h(w_h,w_h)\ge\alpha_h\|w_h\|_V^2$ for every $w_h\in V_h$. For $v_h\in V_h$, define

$$\delta_{a,h}(v_h):=\sup_{w_h\in V_h\setminus\{0\}}\frac{|a(v_h,w_h)-a_h(v_h,w_h)|}{\|w_h\|_V},\qquad \delta_{F,h}:=\sup_{w_h\in V_h\setminus\{0\}}\frac{|F(w_h)-F_h(w_h)|}{\|w_h\|_V}.$$

If $V_h=\{0\}$, both defects are defined to be zero. The load defect $\delta_{F,h}$ includes any source approximation or data oscillation; it is not assumed small or zero without a separate bound.

For a **nonconforming problem**, the exact space $V$ and finite-dimensional trial space $V_h$ need not satisfy $V_h\subseteq V$. Put $X_h:=V+V_h$ and equip it with a norm $\|\cdot\|_h$ whose restrictions to $V$ and $V_h$ are norms. The discrete form $a_h$ is defined on $V_h\times V_h$, and a bounded extension $\widetilde a_h:X_h\times V_h\to\mathbb K$ means $\widetilde a_h=a_h$ on $V_h\times V_h$ and $|\widetilde a_h(z,w_h)|\le M_h\|z\|_h\|w_h\|_h$. For an exact solution $u\in V$, define the nonconforming consistency defect

$$\delta^{\mathrm{nc}}_h(u):=\sup_{w_h\in V_h\setminus\{0\}}\frac{|F_h(w_h)-\widetilde a_h(u,w_h)|}{\|w_h\|_h},$$

with value zero if $V_h=\{0\}$. This residual need not vanish: the exact weak equation is only asserted for tests in $V$.

Geometry and quadrature defects are components of the appropriate form defect when the implemented form is compared with the pulled-back exact form. No exact Galerkin orthogonality is asserted after replacing the form or test space.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\widehat\Omega=(-1,1)^2$ be covered by a finite matching cell mesh, and let $\Phi,\Phi_h$ be continuous geometry maps whose cellwise $C^1$ derivatives satisfy $\|D\Phi\|_\infty+\|D\Phi_h\|_\infty\le M$, $e_0=\|\Phi-\Phi_h\|_\infty$, and $e_1=\|D\Phi-D\Phi_h\|_{L^\infty;op}$. Let $G$ be a scalar physical boundary lift on an open convex neighborhood containing both images and every segment joining corresponding image points, with $\|DG\|_\infty\le L_1$ and $\|D^2G\|_\infty\le L_2$. Define the piecewise pullback gradients by $
abla_{pw}(G\circ\Phi)=D\Phi^T
abla G(\Phi)$ and $
abla_{pw}(G\circ\Phi_h)=D\Phi_h^T
abla G(\Phi_h)$, and set
$$\ell_{\partial,h}(w)=\int_{\widehat\Omega} ig(
abla_{pw}(G\circ\Phi)-
abla_{pw}(G\circ\Phi_h) ig)\cdot
abla w,\qquad w\in H^1_0(\widehat\Omega).$$
With the $H^1$ dual norm, $\|\ell_{\partial,h}\|_{(H^1_0)^*}\le 2(L_1e_1+ML_2e_0)$. Thus the geometry-induced boundary-lift contribution to the Strang load defect is $O(e_0+e_1)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. On $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]]) define $$(u,v)_{H^1}:=(u,v)_{L^2}+\sum_{i=1}^n(D_iu,D_iv)_{L^2},$$ with the $L^2$ inner product of [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. Then $(\cdot,\cdot)_{H^1}$ is an inner product on the Sobolev classes whose induced norm is the $W^{1,2}$ norm of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], and $H^1(\Omega)$ is a Hilbert space for it. The zero-boundary space $H^1_0(\Omega)$ is a closed subspace of $H^1(\Omega)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]) and hence a Hilbert space for the restricted inner product. The pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, in the convention of [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]].

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $F(\widehat x)=A\widehat x+b$ be an affine bijection from a bounded open
set $\widehat K\subset\mathbb R^d$ to $K$, where $A$ is invertible, and let
$1\le p\le\infty$. For every integer $r\ge0$ and scalar
$v\in W^{r,p}(K)$, the pullback $\widehat v:=v\circ F$ belongs to
$W^{r,p}(\widehat K)$. For $r\ge1$ its first weak derivatives satisfy
$$D_{\widehat x_j}\widehat v=\sum_{i=1}^d A_{ij}(D_{x_i}v)\circ F,$$
and higher derivatives are obtained by applying this constant-matrix rule
repeatedly. In particular, for each $0\le m\le r$,
$$|\widehat v|_{W^{m,p}(\widehat K)}\le C(d,m)\|A\|^m|\det A|^{-1/p}|v|_{W^{m,p}(K)},$$
where $|\det A|^{-1/p}:=1$ for $p=\infty$. The reverse estimate holds
with $A^{-1}$ and $|\det A|^{1/p}$ in place of $A$ and
$|\det A|^{-1/p}$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d\ge2$. For every integer $k\ge0$ and
$1\le p\le\infty$, there is a bounded linear operator
$$E_{k,p}:W^{k,p}(\widehat S_d)\longrightarrow W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^d)$$
whose restriction to $\widehat S_d$ is the input class. Consequently
$\widehat S_d$ is a $W^{k,p}$-extension domain in the sense of
[[def-sobolev-extension-domain-and-extension-operator]]. The operator may
be chosen with support in one fixed bounded set.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Then:

1. if $kp<n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every $q$ with $\frac1q\ge\frac1p-\frac kn$ (equivalently $1\le q\le\frac{np}{n-kp}$);
2. if $kp=n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C(q)\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every finite $q$;
3. if $kp>n$, then for every integer $m\ge0$ and every $0<\alpha<1$ with $m+\alpha<k-\frac np$ there is a representative in $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ with $\|u\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$; when $k-\frac np\notin\mathbb Z$ one may take $m=\lfloor k-\frac np\rfloor$ and $\alpha=k-\frac np-m$.

Here $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ uses the continuous derivatives of the constructed representative on an ambient neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$, with norm
$$\|g\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\sum_{|\beta|\le m}\sup_{\overline\Omega}|D^\beta g|+\sum_{|\beta|=m}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|D^\beta g(x)-D^\beta g(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}.$$
For $\Omega=\varnothing$ set these norm values to $0$. The proof supplies such an ambient representative, so no boundary differentiability or regularity of $\partial\Omega$ is assumed.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k\ge1$, $1\le p\le\infty$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a
bounded $C^k$ domain in the graph sense of
[[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]. Then for every open set
$V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $\overline\Omega\subseteq V$ there is a bounded
linear extension operator
$$E:W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)\longrightarrow W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K),\qquad (Eu)|_\Omega=u\ \text{a.e. on }\Omega,$$
such that $\operatorname{supp}(Eu)$ is a compact subset of $V$ for every
$u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. In particular each bounded $C^k$ domain is a
$W^{k,p}$-extension domain, with an operator whose output is supported in any
prescribed neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$. For $k=0$, extension by zero
is an isometric $L^p$ extension on any open $\Omega$; its output is supported
in the compact set $\overline\Omega\subseteq V$ when $\Omega$ is bounded.

Assume Countable Choice. For any open $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$,
$n\ge1$, any $1\le p\le\infty$ and any
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, extension by zero
$$E_0u(x)=u(x)\ \ (x\in\Omega),\qquad E_0u(x)=0\ \ (x\notin\Omega),$$
acted on representatives, sends $W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ linearly into
$W^{1,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$. For every $u\in W_0^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
and every coordinate direction $i$, the class $D_i(E_0u)$ is the zero
extension of the class $D_iu$, and every $L^p$ component norm is preserved:
$$\|E_0u\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}=\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)},\qquad \|D_i(E_0u)\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}=\|D_iu\|_{L^p(\Omega)},$$
so that $\|E_0u\|_{W^{1,p}(\mathbb R^n)}=\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge2$, $d=n-1$, $1\le p<\infty$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$H=\{x=(x',x_n)\in\mathbb R^n:x_n>0\}$ with
$\partial H=\mathbb R^d\times\{0\}$. Write $\partial_n$ for the last
coordinate derivative.

(i) For every $u\in C(\overline H)\cap W^{1,p}(H;\mathbb K)$ with compact
support, the classical boundary function $g=u(\cdot,0)$ satisfies
$$|g(x')|^p\le p\int_0^\infty|u(x',t)|^{p-1}\,|\partial_nu(x',t)|\,dt$$
for a.e. $x'\in\mathbb R^d$, hence
$\|g\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^d)}^p\le p\,\|u\|_{L^p(H)}^{p-1}\|\partial_nu\|_{L^p(H)}\le p\,\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}^p$.
For every $h>0$ the strip form
$$h\,|g(x')|^p\le C_p\Bigl(\int_0^h|u(x',t)|^pdt+h^p\int_0^h|\partial_nu(x',t)|^pdt\Bigr)$$
holds for a.e. $x'$, with $C_p=2^{p-1}$ for $1<p<\infty$ and $C_1=1$.

(ii) There is a unique bounded linear operator
$T_+:W^{1,p}(H;\mathbb K)\to L^p(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb K)$ with
$T_+u=u(\cdot,0)$ for every compactly supported
$u\in C(\overline H)\cap W^{1,p}(H)$, and
$\|T_+u\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^d)}\le C(n,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}$; it is the unique
bounded extension of classical restriction, and $T_+u$ depends only on the
a.e. class of $u$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p<\infty$ and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then the compactly supported smooth
functions $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ are dense in
$W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$: for every
$u\in W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ and every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ with
$$\|\varphi-u\|_{W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n)}<\delta.$$
No such norm-density assertion is made for $p=\infty$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$
If $F:M\to N$ and $G:N\to P$ are smooth, then $d(G\circ F)_p=dG_{F(p)}\circ dF_p$ for every $p\in M$.

Let $n \ge 1$, **assume the Axiom of Countable Choice**
([[def-countable-choice]]), and let $a_i \le b_i$ be reals for $i<n$. Write

$$R^{\circ} := \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_i < x_i < b_i \text{ for every } i<n \,\}, \qquad \overline{R} := [a,b] = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^n : a_i \le x_i \le b_i \text{ for every } i<n \,\}$$

([[def-multidimensional-rectangle-and-volume]]). Then $R^{\circ}$ is open and
$\overline{R}$ is closed, so both are Borel and Lebesgue measurable, and **every**
set $R$ with $R^{\circ} \subseteq R \subseteq \overline{R}$ is Lebesgue
measurable with

$$\lambda_n(R) \;=\; \prod_{i<n}(b_i-a_i).$$

In particular this covers the four one-dimensional face conventions in each
coordinate — the open box, the closed box $[a,b]$, the half-open box
$B(a,b) = \prod_{i<n}(a_i,b_i]$ of [[def-half-open-box]], and every mixture of
them, in any combination of coordinates — and it gives measure $0$ to all of them
whenever $a_i = b_i$ for some $i<n$. For a half-open box with infinite
parameters the value is already
$\lambda_n(B) = \operatorname{vol}(B)$ ([[thm-lebesgue-measure-is-a-complete-measure]]).

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$\eta\in C^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and
$u\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. For
$\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n$, suppose that for every $\gamma\le\alpha$ there is
$v_\gamma\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$D^\gamma u=v_\gamma$ weakly. Then $\eta u$ has a weak $\alpha$-derivative,
and its almost-everywhere class is
$$D^\alpha(\eta u)=\sum_{\beta\le\alpha}\binom{\alpha}{\beta}(D^\beta\eta)D^{\alpha-\beta}u\quad\text{in }L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K).$$
where $D^\beta\eta$ is the classical derivative and products are pointwise
products of representatives. The resulting class does not depend on the
representatives.

For $k\in\mathbb N_0$ and $1\le p\le\infty$, if
$u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and $D^\beta\eta\in L^\infty(\Omega)$ for
every $|\beta|\le k$, then $\eta u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and the same
formula holds in $L^p$ for every $|\alpha|\le k$. In particular,
$\eta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ is a sufficient condition on the
multiplier for this global conclusion.

For $\Omega=\varnothing$ all classes are zero and the identity holds. The
pairing convention is bilinear, with no complex conjugation.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded polyhedral open set with a finite matching
affine simplicial mesh, let $1\le p<\infty$, and let $v$ be a real-valued
conforming piecewise polynomial whose polynomial trace vanishes on every boundary
facet. Then
$$v\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega),\qquad \|v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|\nabla v\|_{L^p(\Omega)}.$$
Here $W^{1,p}_0$ is the norm closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$; no C1
trace characterization is used.
Let $0<r<R$ and $n\ge 1$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:\mathbb R^n\to [0,1]$ such that $\rho=1$ on $\overline B_r(0)$ and $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq B_R(0)$.

Fix an integer $d\ge2$. The **reference open simplex** is
$$\widehat S_d:=\{\widehat x\in\mathbb R^d:\widehat x_i>0\ (1\le i\le d),\ \sum_{i=1}^d\widehat x_i<1\},$$
with closure $\overline{\widehat S_d}=\operatorname{conv}\{0,e_1,\ldots,e_d\}$.

A **matching affine simplicial mesh** of a bounded polyhedral open set
$\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ is a finite set $\mathcal T$ of closed,
nondegenerate $d$-simplices such that their union is $\overline\Omega$,
their interiors are pairwise disjoint, $\Omega$ is the interior of their
union, and the intersection of two distinct cells is either empty or a
whole face of each. Thus no lower-dimensional crack is omitted from
$\Omega$ while its surrounding cells are retained. Every interior facet is
incident to exactly two cells and every boundary facet to one. The faces of
a cell are the convex hulls of its vertex subsets. A facet means a face of
dimension $d-1$.

For each cell $K\in\mathcal T$, an affine bijection
$$F_K:\overline{\widehat S_d}\to K,\qquad F_K(\widehat x)=b_K+A_K\widehat x,$$
with invertible $A_K\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is a **reference map**.
Choose the vertex order so $\det A_K>0$; this is the orientation convention
used for Piola formulas. Write $h_K:=\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and let
$\rho_K$ be the radius of the largest Euclidean ball contained in $K$.
A family $\{\mathcal T_h\}_{h\in H}$ is **shape regular** if there is a
finite $\sigma$ such that $h_K/\rho_K\le\sigma$ for every
$h\in H$ and $K\in\mathcal T_h$. This universal condition is vacuous for
an empty family.
This definition uses radius; references using the diameter of the inscribed
ball differ by a factor of two.

An affine image of the reference square is a parallelogram. A general

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: For each mesh triangle $K$, apply [F1] to pull $u|_K$ back to the reference triangle, and then apply [F2]. This gives a continuous representative on $\overline K$. It is unique: if two continuous representatives differed at one point, continuity would make them differ on a nonempty open subset of $K$, contradicting [F6]. Thus each cellwise nodal value is individually well-defined.

Put $z=E_0u$, the zero extension from [F3]. On either side of any straight line, the half-space trace is obtained from the positive-half-space trace in [F4] by a translation and, when needed, a reflection; [F5] verifies that these changes preserve the Sobolev class and norm. The two traces of a global $H^1(\mathbb R^2)$ class across such a line agree: choose $z_m\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ converging to $z$ by [F4]; the two traces of each $z_m$ are its same classical restriction, and boundedness of the two trace maps passes this equality to the limit. On the exterior half-space of each side of $\Omega$, $z=0$, so both its exterior trace and its interior trace are zero.

If $K_+$ and $K_-$ share an interior edge, every point $x$ in the relative interior of that edge has a ball $B\subset\Omega$ meeting only those two cells. By [F2], $u|_B$ has a continuous representative. On each of the two open half-balls $B\cap K_\pm$, this representative and the corresponding representative from step 1.1 agree almost everywhere, hence everywhere by [F6]. Taking limits to $x$ shows the two cell values agree at $x$; continuity along the closed edge gives agreement at its endpoints as well. For an interior mesh vertex, take a ball about the vertex contained in $\Omega$ and repeat this argument for every incident cell.

Let $x$ lie in the relative interior of a boundary mesh edge $E$. Choose a ball $B$ centered at $x$ small enough that its interior half-ball lies in the unique incident triangle $K$ and its other boundary is disjoint from all mesh edges. By [F9] choose $\chi\in C_c^\infty(B)$ equal to one near $x$. On the interior half-space define $v=\chi u_K$ inside $B$ and zero outside, where $u_K$ is the continuous cell representative from step 1.1. The cutoff vanishes near the circular part of $\partial B$, so the weak test identity shows $v\in H^1$ of that half-space; it is compactly supported and continuous on the closed half-space. Its class is $\chi z$ there. By linearity and boundedness of the trace, and by approximation with the smooth functions in step 1.2, $T(\chi z)=\chi Tz=0$ on the side. The classical-restriction clause of [F4] gives $T v=\chi u_K|_E$, so $u_K=0$ almost everywhere near $x$ on $E$. Continuity from step 1.1 makes this value zero at every point of that edge, including its endpoints.

Interior edge values agree by step 2.1. At a boundary vertex, the incident triangles form a connected fan because the square is convex; the fan is a chain under adjacency across edges containing that vertex, and at least one end cell has a boundary edge. Step 2.2 gives zero at the vertex in that end cell, and step 2.1 propagates that value through the fan. Thus all cell values at every shared vertex agree and boundary vertex values are zero. The affine traces of adjacent P1 interpolants agree because they agree at both edge endpoints, so $I_hu$ is continuous; on each boundary edge it is affine with both endpoint values zero, hence its trace is zero. Apply [F8] to conclude $I_hu\in H^1_0(\Omega)$.
